- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and overshoots peak; reduce forecast slope after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates and fails to capture sharp declines; increase downward bias in early horizon.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day average by 1–2% in early cycles; apply 1.5–2x smoothing or adjust mean reversion target downward.
- After a price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often fails to correct downward within 5–7 days; apply lagged correction rule: subtract 0.5–1.0 from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates true drop in 3rd–5th week of forecast horizon; apply “early drop correction” by adding 0.5–1.0 to forecast at 10–15 day mark if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward bias at 15–20 day horizon.
